content:
oliver: heads-up: we started a canary for preemptive-stream-emit in us-east-1 at 10:00. idea: emit the first token chunk immediately using a cheap quant path so streaming clients see the very first byte faster.

tara: baseline numbers? curious about startup latency and any downstream impact on throughput.

oliver: short snapshot (10:00-10:30, 7% traffic): startup-p50 42ms -> 18ms (-57%), startup-p95 340ms -> 165ms (-52%). steady-state token throughput unchanged. estimated token-cost -8% due to reduced idle GPU time during open streams.

kevin: nice. any quality regressions for the first chunk? sometimes initial framing changes result in bad completions.

oliver: we ran the stream-init eval set (2.5k samples). automated checks show no meaningful drift. one pattern: when prompts include multi-sentence system instructions, the first-token summary occasionally lost a comma; we fixed by delaying emit for prompts with >200 system tokens.

deploy-bot: rollout: stream-controller v3.2.1 -> canary(7%) (build b-20260305-11)

mira: will this affect Dedicated hosts or billing?

oliver: no pool changes; scheduling still honors Dedicated placement. billing unchanged. console will show a new "stream startup latency" metric in Route Analytics.

ops-bot: alert rule added: stream-preemptive/startup-p95 > baseline*1.6 -> ping @eng-oncall @eng-runtime
tara: rollback criteria?

oliver: auto-rollback if startup errors increase > baseline*2 for 5m OR startup-p95 > baseline*1.7 for 3m. manual rollback if dogfood flags continuity issues. ramp: 7% -> 35% in 12h -> 100% in 48h if stable.

kevin: can we add a synthetic stream test for system-instruction prompts? want early catch on the comma/loss case.

mira: added. also tagging product for a short blurb in the weekly update.

oliver: thanks all. action items: add console tile (oliver), extended evals (kevin), monitor canary and synthetic tests (ops-bot). :rocket:
